@@ -184,6 +184,47 @@ Use the TypeScript template when you need the most operationally rich
 template profile, including package-manager detection and separate MCP
 overlays for authoring and build artifacts.
 
-See xref:page$repository/docs/template_typescript.adoc[TypeScript Template]
-for package-manager detection, dual MCP overlays, and customization
-guidance.
+Package-manager detection:
+
+. `bun.lockb` or `bun.lock`
+. `pnpm-lock.yaml`
+. `yarn.lock`
+. `package-lock.json` or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`
+. `npm` when no lockfile exists
+
+This keeps the generated `Makefile` lockfile-first instead of choosing
+Bun only because it happens to be installed on the local machine.
+
+Generated targets:
+
+* `make install`
+* `make build`
+* `make test`
+* `make check`
+* `make lint`
+* `make verify`
+* `make certify`
+
+TypeScript keeps `install` separate from `build`. Build commands should
+not implicitly mutate dependency state. `make lint` and `make check`
+skip with an explicit message when the corresponding package scripts are
+not present. `make certify` runs the package-manager `certify` script
+when one exists and otherwise falls back to `make verify`.
+
+Default MCP view:
+
+* `cx-mcp.toml` stays source-oriented for `src/**`, workspace metadata,
+  and key TypeScript config files
+* `cx-mcp-build.toml` stays build-oriented for `dist/**` plus minimal
+  package metadata
+
+Use the source-oriented overlay for live editing and code
+understanding. Use the build overlay when you want to inspect emitted
+artifacts without broadening the default authoring surface.
+
+Customize the generated overlays if your repository:
+
+* uses a source root other than `src/`
+* emits artifacts outside `dist/`
+* stores important workspace metadata in additional files
+* needs stricter excludes for framework-specific caches

-= TypeScript Template
-:page-layout: default
-
-
-The TypeScript `cx init` template is designed to be source-first for
-authoring workflows and lockfile-first for package-manager selection.
-
-=== Package Manager Detection
-
-The generated `Makefile` chooses a package manager in this order:
-
-. `bun.lockb` or `bun.lock`
-. `pnpm-lock.yaml`
-. `yarn.lock`
-. `package-lock.json` or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`
-. `npm` when no lockfile exists
-
-This avoids choosing Bun only because it happens to be installed on the
-local machine.
-
-=== Generated Targets
-
-The TypeScript `Makefile` normalizes these targets:
-
-* `make install`
-* `make build`
-* `make test`
-* `make check`
-* `make lint`
-* `make verify`
-* `make certify`
-
-`install` is intentionally separate from `build`. Build commands should
-not implicitly mutate dependency state. `make lint` and `make check`
-skip with an explicit message when the corresponding package scripts are
-not present. `make certify` runs the package-manager `certify` script
-when one exists and otherwise falls back to `make verify`.
-
-=== MCP Overlays
-
-`cx init --template typescript` generates two MCP overlays:
-
-* `cx-mcp.toml` Source-oriented authoring overlay for `src/**`,
-workspace metadata, and key TypeScript config files.
-* `cx-mcp-build.toml` Build-artifact overlay for `dist/**` plus
-minimal package metadata.
-
-Use the source-oriented overlay for live editing and code understanding.
-Use the build overlay when you want to inspect emitted artifacts without
-broadening the default authoring surface. Edit the authoring and build
-overlays independently when your repository uses nonstandard source or
-output layouts.
-
-=== When To Customize
-
-Adjust the generated overlays if your repository:
-
-* uses a source root other than `src/`
-* emits artifacts outside `dist/`
-* stores important workspace metadata in additional files
-* needs stricter excludes for framework-specific caches
